candidate_visible.claim_text: The alignment tax of constitutional AI approaches is negligible compared to RLHF.
candidate_visible.evidence_text: The evidence consists of a single unreplicated study with high variance (n=5). No confidence intervals reported. The study does not control for model size, training data, or evaluation methodology.

candidate_visible.claim_text: Few-shot prompting in GPT-4 surpasses fine-tuned BERT on all biomedical NLP tasks.
candidate_visible.evidence_text: The evidence compares GPT-4 on 3 tasks to BERT on 3 different tasks. Tasks are not the same. Evaluation metrics differ. The study is a preprint with no peer review.

candidate_visible.claim_text: LLM-based evaluation metrics achieve higher correlation with human judgment than all existing automatic metrics for text generation.
candidate_visible.evidence_text: The evidence reports correlations on 2 datasets using 1 LLM (GPT-4) as evaluator, compared to 3 baselines. No confidence intervals, no statistical significance tests, no analysis of evaluator bias.

candidate_visible.claim_text: Retrieval-augmented generation reduces hallucination rates in clinical question answering.
candidate_visible.evidence_text: The cited work is peer-reviewed, reports n=1,842 dialogues with 95% confidence intervals, and finds a statistically significant reduction in hallucination on open-domain conversational QA. The clinical setting is not evaluated: no clinical corpus, no clinician adjudication, and no patient-safety endpoint appears in the study design.
candidate_visible.source_text: Shuster et al. (2021) Retrieval Augmentation Reduces Hallucination in Conversation

candidate_visible.claim_text: Chain-of-thought prompting improves arithmetic reasoning in models under 10B parameters.
candidate_visible.evidence_text: The cited work is peer-reviewed and reports gains on GSM8K with confidence intervals across several model families. Every reported arithmetic result is at 62B parameters or above, and the paper states that chain-of-thought yields no gain, and can hurt, at smaller scales. No model under 10B parameters is reported on the arithmetic benchmarks.
candidate_visible.source_text: Wei et al. (2022) Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models

candidate_visible.claim_text: Sparse autoencoders recover monosemantic features in production language models.
candidate_visible.evidence_text: The cited work reports dictionary-learning results with quantitative reconstruction metrics and an interpretability evaluation. The subject is a one-layer transformer trained for the study. The claim concerns production language models; the evidence reports no result at that scale, and the authors describe the setting as a simplified testbed.
candidate_visible.source_text: Bricken et al. (2023) Towards Monosemanticity: Decomposing Language Models With Dictionary Learning
